items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4472

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the banking law and the tax law, in
relation to establishing the NY ABLE act

PURPOSE:  The intent of this act is to encourage and assist
individuals and families in saving private funds for the purpose of
supporting individuals with disabilities to maintain health,
independence and quality of life; and to provide secure funding for
disability related expenses on behalf of designated beneficiaries with
disabilities that will supplement, but not supplant, benefits provided
through existing sources.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 is the short title,.

Section 2 is the legislative intent for the creation of ABLE accounts.

Section 3 amends the banking law by adding a new article 2-D.

90-a. Establishes definitions for this act.

90-b. Requires the superintendent of the department of financial
services to establish NY ABLE account plan for all eligible
individuals with the goal and purpose of supporting individuals with
disabilities to maintain health, independence, and quality of life.

90-c. Creates a NY ABLE account advisory committee, in which members
will be appointing in consultation with the New York State Department
of Health, the office of Mental Health, Office for persons with
developmental disabilities, and the members shall be appointed for
three years.

Members on the committee must have knowledge, skill, and expertise in
issues relating to, individuals with disabilities.

90-d. Provides the program requirements.

90-e. Provided distribution requirements for NY ABLE accounts.

90-f. Powers of the Comptroller to implement the NY ABLE savings
account program.

Section 4 amends section 237 of the banking law to designate the
superintendent of financial services to promulgate rules and
regulations to allow a savings bank to act as trustee of an ABLE
account.

Section 5 amends subsection (c) of section 612 of the tax law is
amended by adding two new paragraphs.

Section 6 is the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:  The purpose of this legislation is to create New York
State Achieving Better Life Experience (ABLE) accounts to encourage
and assist individuals and families in saving private funds for the


purpose of supporting individuals with intellectual and developmental
disabilities to maintain health, independence and quality of life.
The passage of this legislation is critical to help fund a variety of
essential expenses for individuals living with disabilities.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: Similar to S.7937-2014

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: Minimal.

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect on the one hundred
eightieth day after it shall become a law; provided, however, that
effective immediately, the addition, amendment and/or repeal of any
rules or regulations necessary for the implementation of this act on
its effective date are authorized and directed to be made and
completed on or before such effective date.

BILL NUMBER:S4472A

TITLE OF BILL:

An  act  to  amend the banking law, the social services law, the tax law
and the civil practice law and rules, in relation to establishing the NY
ABLE act

PURPOSE:

The intent of this act is to encourage and assist individuals and  fami-
lies  in  saving private funds for the purpose of supporting individuals
with disabilities to maintain health, independence and quality of  life;
and  to provide secure funding for disability related expenses on behalf
of designated beneficiaries with disabilities that will supplement,  but
not supplant, benefits provided through existing sources.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 is the short title.

Section 2 is the legislative intent for the creation of ABLE accounts.

Section 3 amends the banking law by adding a new article 2-D.

90-a. Establishes definitions for this act.

90-b. Requires the comptroller in consultation with the commissioners of
the  office  of  mental health, the office for people with developmental
disabilities, and the department of health to establish NY ABLE  account
plan  for all eligible individuals with the goal and purpose of support-
ing individuals with disabilities to maintain health, independence,  and
quality of life.

90-c.  Creates a NY ABLE account advisory council which shall consist of
the following members or their designee's; the comptroller, the  commis-
sioner  of  the  office of mental health, the commissioner of the office
for people with developmental  disabilities,  the  commissioner  of  the
department  of  health, the superintended of the department of financial
services, the commissioner of the department of  taxation  and  finance,
the  commissioner  of  temporary  disability assistance. In addition the
governor shall appoint three members, the  temporary  president  of  the
senate and speaker of the assembly shall each appoint two members.

Members  of  the  council  shall  have knowledge, skill and expertise in
issues relating to individuals with disabilities;  expertise  in  issues
relating  to  individuals  with  disabilities;  expertise in services to
persons with disabilities; and knowledge in management  and  support  of
the fiscal affairs of such persons with disabilities.

90-d. Provides the program requirements.

90-e. Provided distribution requirements for NY ABLE accounts.

90-f. Powers of the Comptroller to implement the NY ABLE savings account
program.

Section  4 amends section 237 of the banking law to designate the super-
intendent of financial services to promulgate rules and  regulations  to
allow a savings bank to act as trustee of an ABLE account.

Section  5 amends subdivisions 7 of section 100-c of the banking law, as
amended by chapter 134 of the laws of 2002 to include NY ABLE accounts.

Section 6 amends subsection (c) of section 612 of the tax law is amended
by adding two new paragraphs.

Section 7 amends subparagraph 2 of paragraph  b  of  subdivisions  2  of
section 366 of the social services law.

Section 8 amends subdivision j of section 5205 of the civil practice law
and rules.

Section 6 is the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

The  purpose  of  this legislation is to create New York State Achieving
Better Life Experience (ABLE) accounts to encourage and assist  individ-
uals  and families in saving private funds for the purpose of supporting
individuals with disabilities, including  those  with  intellectual  and
developmental  disabilities to maintain health, independence and quality
of life. The passage of this legislation is  critical  to  help  fund  a
variety of essential expenses for individuals living with disabilities.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

Similar to S.7937-2014

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Minimal.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This  act  shall  take  effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall become a law; provided, however, that effective  immediately,  the
addition,  amendment and/or repeal of any rules or regulations necessary
for the implementation of this act on its effective date are  authorized
and directed to be made and completed on or before such effective date.

BILL NUMBER:  S4472C

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the mental hygiene law, the tax law
and the social services law, in relation to establishing the NY ABLE
act

 PURPOSE :

The intent of this act is to encourage and assist individuals and
families in saving private funds for the purpose of supporting
individuals with disabilities to maintain health, independence and
quality of life; and to provide secure funding for disability related
expenses on behalf of designated beneficiaries with disabilities that
will supplement, but not supplant, benefits provided through existing
sources.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 is the short title.

Section 2 is the legislative intent for the creation of NY ABLE
accounts.

Section 3 amends the mental hygiene law by adding a new article 84.

84.03 - Establishes definitions for this act.

84.05 - Authorizes the comptroller to establish NY ABLE accounts for
all eligible individuals with the goal and purpose of supporting
individuals with disabilities to maintain health, independence, and
quality of life. Furthermore, it authorizes the comptroller to
promulgate any and all rules and regulations necessary for the
implementation of this article in consultation with the commissioners
of the office of mental health, the office for people with
developmental disabilities, and the department of health.

84.07 - Creates a NY ABLE account advisory council which shall consist
of the following members or their designee's; the comptroller, the
commissioner of the office of mental health, the commissioner of the
office for people with developmental disabilities, the commissioner of
the department of health, the superintended of the department of
financial services, the commissioner of the department of taxation and
finance, the commissioner of temporary disability assistance. In
addition the governor shall appoint three members, the temporary
president of the senate and speaker of the assembly shall each appoint
two members.

Members of the council shall have knowledge, skill and expertise in
issues relating to individuals with disabilities; expertise in issues
relating to individuals with disabilities; expertise in services to
persons with disabilities; and knowledge in management and support of
the fiscal affairs of such persons with disabilities.

84.09 - Provides the program requirements.

84.11 - Provided distribution requirements for NY ABLE accounts.

Section 4 amends subsection (b) of section 612 of the tax law is
amended by adding a new paragraph.

Section 5 amends subsection (c) of section 612 of the tax law by
adding two new paragraphs.

Section 6 amends paragraph (a) of subdivision 2 of section 366 of the
social services law by adding a new subparagraph 11.

Section 7 is the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

On December 19th, 2014, President Barack Obama signed into law the
Achieving a Better Life Experience (ABLE) Act, authorizing states to
establish ABLE savings accounts for qualified individuals with
disabilities. One of the most important benefits of the ABLE savings
account is that money deposited into the account will be exempt from
the monetary limit related to personal assets that if exceeded in most
cases, would deem the individual account owner ineligible for Medicaid
and Supplemental Security income benefits. Furthermore, ABLE savings
accounts offer families the benefits of a tax deferred financial
vehicle.

As the state continues to transition away from institutional settings
and emphasize community based and least restrictive treatment models
for people with disabilities, New York must utilize all available
tools in order to ensure the success of every individual with a
disability. This bill will foster independence, improved quality of
life, and better maintenance of health for individuals with
disabilities and their families by authorizing New York State to
establish ABLE savings accounts.

The passage of this legislation is critical to help fund a variety of
essential expenses for individuals living with disabilities.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

Similar to S.7937-2014

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Minimal.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect April 1, 2016; provided, however, that
effective immediately, the addition, amendment and/or repeal of any
rules or regulations necessary for the implementation of this act on
its effective date are authorized and directed to be made and
completed on or before such effective date.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 30 Chapter 576

       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 4472-D, entitled:

    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the mental hygiene law, the tax law, the social
        services law and the state finance law, in  relation  to  estab-
        lishing the NY ABLE act"

    APPROVED

  This  bill  would establish a NY ABLE account -- a savings account for
persons with developmental disabilities to use  for  non-Medicaid  reim-
bursable  expenses  during  their  adult  lives.  The funds would accrue
interest tax-free and would not be a factor for Medicaid eligibility.

  I fully support the intent of this bill. For parents who have a  child
with  a  disability, saving for that child's future care may enable them
to rest easy knowing their child will be  cared  for  during  adulthood.
Moreover,  I  recognize that Medicaid does not cover all expenses neces-
sary to live a full and independent life, and that a NY ABLE account may
enable children with disabilities some degree of financial  freedom  and
comfort into adulthood. I applaud the advocacy groups who have fought so
hard to make these accounts a reality throughout the United States and I
am  proud that today, New York will join those states that allow for the
creation of ABLE accounts.

  However, this bill has significant unbudgeted fiscal implications  due
to the potentially large tax deductions associated with contributions to
these  accounts. I am fully committed to working with the Legislature to
explore how we can create a framework for incorporating appropriate  and
fiscally  responsible  deductions  in  the  context of the broader State
budget. The Legislature has agreed to a  chapter  amendment  to  address
this issue. On this basis, I am signing this bill.

  This bill is approved.                      (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO

                                ______

summary: Establishes the New York achieving a better life experience (NY ABLE) savings account act to support individuals with disabilities to maintain health, independence and quality of life.
